title: The soul was never yours to keep
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 188
summary: The shabad begins by unsettling possessive grief: relations are named, but ownership is false. It moves through Hukam, shared dust and breath, and ends when the Guru opens the shutters of doubt.
whyItMatters: This speaks to the person overwhelmed by loss, panic, or the cry of mine. Taken seriously, it does not belittle sorrow, but it stops grief from turning into possession.
takeaway: Let this stay with you: let grief answer to Hukam instead of ownership.

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਾ ਕੀ ਮਾਈ ਕਾ ਕੋ ਬਾਪ ॥
lines.transliteration: kaa kee maiee kaa ko baap ||
lines.translation: Whose mother is this? Whose father is this?
They are relatives in name only- they are all false. ||1||
Why are you screaming and shouting, you fool?

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਿਲਿ ਸੰਜੋਗਿ ਹੁਕਮਿ ਤੂੰ ਆਇਆ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: mil sa(n)jog hukam too(n) aaiaa ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: By good destiny and the Lord's Order, you have come into the world. ||1||Pause||
There is the one dust, the one light,
the one praanic wind. Why are you crying? For whom do you cry? ||2||
People weep and cry out, ""Mine, mine!""
Says Nanak, the Guru has opened my shutters;
I am liberated, and my doubts have been dispelled. ||4||43||112||

structure: First, it begins by exposing how quickly the mind tries to own what was never its possession.
Then, it breaks the illusion further through one dust, one light, and one breath moving through all.
Finally, it ends with the Guru opening the inner shutters until doubt gives way to release.
